metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Thermal Energy — Matching Solar Water Heater Features to Thermal Principles
metadata.note: Figure 3 shows a natural convection solar water heating system. Features: black surface (good absorber), copper tubing (good conductor), glass cover (greenhouse effect), water/pipe loop (convection). 4 slots × 1m each. Caribbean context: solar water heating is widely used across the Caribbean. Word bank: 6 tokens (4 correct features + 2 distractors).

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q2a — Solar Heater Features and Thermal Principles
question.text:
The diagram (Figure 3) shows a natural convection solar water heating system with the following components: a solar collector with a black surface, copper tubing, a glass cover, an insulated backing, and a hot-water tank connected by pipes carrying water in a loop.

State which feature of the solar water heating system demonstrates EACH of the following thermal energy principles. (4 marks)

Thermal Energy PrincipleFeature of the System
(i) Good absorption of heat[[1]]
(ii) Heat transfer by convection[[2]]
(iii) The greenhouse effect[[3]]
(iv) Good heat transfer by conduction[[4]]
question.general_feedback:
Feature–principle matching:

  • (i) Good absorption of heat → Black surface — Dark/black surfaces absorb radiation most efficiently; matt black is the best absorber across all wavelengths.
  • (ii) Heat transfer by convection → Water/pipe loop (connecting tank to collector) — Hot water (less dense) rises from the collector into the tank; cooler water sinks back through the return pipe — natural convection current.
  • (iii) The greenhouse effect → Glass cover — Glass transmits short-wave solar radiation inward but absorbs/reflects longer-wave infrared radiation emitted by the heated surfaces, trapping heat (the greenhouse effect).
  • (iv) Good heat transfer by conduction → Copper tubing — Copper is an excellent thermal conductor; heat transfers rapidly from the sun-heated tubing walls into the water flowing inside.

groups.label: Feature that maximises heat absorption
groups.diagnostic_hint: The BLACK surface of the solar collector absorbs maximum radiation. Black surfaces are the best absorbers of infrared radiation (they are also the best emitters).

options.text: Black surface of the solar collector
Water flowing through the pipe loop
Glass cover over the solar collector
Copper tubing inside the collector
Insulation lining the sides and bottom
Hot-water storage tank at the top

groups.label: Feature that transfers heat to the domestic supply
groups.diagnostic_hint: WATER flows through the pipe loop, absorbing heat from the collector and carrying it to the storage tank. Water's high specific heat capacity makes it an excellent heat-transfer fluid.

options.text: Black surface of the solar collector
Water flowing through the pipe loop
Glass cover over the solar collector
Copper tubing inside the collector
Insulation lining the sides and bottom
Hot-water storage tank at the top

groups.label: Feature that reduces convection heat loss
groups.diagnostic_hint: The GLASS cover traps heat inside the collector (greenhouse effect) and reduces convection heat loss from the black absorber surface to the outside air.

options.text: Black surface of the solar collector
Water flowing through the pipe loop
Glass cover over the solar collector
Copper tubing inside the collector
Insulation lining the sides and bottom
Hot-water storage tank at the top

groups.label: Feature that conducts heat efficiently from absorber to water
groups.diagnostic_hint: COPPER tubing is used because copper has very high thermal conductivity — heat is rapidly conducted from the black absorber plate into the water flowing through the pipes.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 6 tokens for 4 slots; 4 correct + 2 distractors. 'Insulation lining' — this PREVENTS heat loss (good insulator, not conductor); students may confuse insulation with conduction. 'Hot-water storage tank' — it stores hot water (thermal storage/inertia) but is not the primary demonstrator of any of the 4 listed principles. Key distractor trap: students sometimes choose glass for 'good absorption' (glass does absorb some IR) but the specific CSEC answer for absorption is the black surface.
